items.title: [fsdp, model] fix: run fused LM heads through FSDP2 hooks
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8091. With untied embeddings, FSDP2 shards `lm_head` independently, but fused forwards read its weight from the parent. This bypasses the head's unsharding, mixed precision, CPU offload and backward hooks. A two-GPU Qwen3 reproducer fails with mixed Tensor/DTensor operands (Torch), BF16/FP32 operands (Triton), or CPU weights under offload.

Run the fused projection through an FSDP-registered forward method on the existing head. The head keeps its own sharding group and ordinary logits `forward`; backend selection and label preparation remain unchanged. The dense, Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5 and GLM4V adapters share this entry point.

Related work: closed #7427 instead keeps the fused head in the root FSDP unit. Open #8004 adds an opt-in FP32 head and routes that branch through its head forward, while the default fused path still reads the weight directly. Open #5948 falls back to materialized logits for a sharded Qwen3-VL Torch head; this change retains fused computation and also fixes the default dense and other adapter paths. It does not implement #8090's Triton shape change or #7323's visual-call alignment.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+FSDP+fused
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

On two RTX 5090 GPUs, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Transformers 5.6.1 and Liger 0.8.2:

```bash
python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 -m pytest -sv tests/special_distributed/test_fused_lm_head_fsdp2.py
# 144 passed on each rank (144 distributed cases, not 288 independent tests)
```

The matrix covers six small random model configurations, Torch/Triton/Liger, tied/untied heads, CPU offload on/off, two accumulated micro-batches per update, two updates, and no-grad inference. Outputs, all trainable gradients and updated parameters are compared with both ordinary HF logits and the same fused arithmetic

# [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training

## Problem

RL + LoRA workflows have three vLLM-side issues:

1. **sleep/wake crash**: Level-2 sleep with `enable_lora=True` crashes with KeyError — LoRA adapter parameters are not in cumem's tag set ([#39934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39934))

3. **LoRA + MoE mismatch**: logprob divergence between training and inference grows with LoRA rank on MoE models (Qwen3.6, GLM-4.7-Flash) ([SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776))

## Downstream demand

- [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975): Adapter-only vLLM LoRA sync for GRPO/AsyncGRPO
- [SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776): LoRA + MoE inference mismatch investigation
- [verl#6782](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6782): Qwen3.5-27B LoRA GRPO — vLLM never emits EOS with rank=64

## Exit criterion

- sleep/wake + LoRA (#39934) no longer crashes
- Adapter-only sync path available (no full-weight merge required)

Two weeks from posting.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache: backend advertises a kernel block size the kernels do not use
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On ROCm, the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool sparse indexer **silently overwrites its own KV cache**. 4096 pool entries are written into 864 distinct slots, so ~79 % of the indexer's keys are wrong. The model still produces fluent text, so nothing crashes — long-context recall just degrades, and `temperature=0` stops being reproducible because the damage depends on which physical blocks the allocator hands out.

This is **ROCm-only** and distinct from #40018 (whose fix, #43781, is present in the tree I tested).

### Root cause

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
return [1, MultipleOf(16)] if current_platform.is_rocm() else [64]
```

On CUDA the backend declares exactly `[64]`, so vLLM sets `kernel_block_size = 64`, `BlockTable.use_hybrid_blocks = True`, and builds a kernel-granular block table. On ROCm it declares "any multiple of 16", so the hybrid aligner's choice (640 tokens here) is taken as natively supported: `blocks_per_kv_block == 1`, **no kernel-granular block table**.

But the kernels do not read 640-token blocks. DeepGEMM/AITER paged-MQA reads pool pages of 32 states; with `tokens_per_state == index_kpool == 4` that is 128 tokens. So the storage block (640 tok = 160 states) is five pages, and both `slot_mapping` and `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` address it with the **page** size (32) while the block table holds **spec-block** ids — a 5x over-subscription.

The intended split is even documented in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py` as `storage_kernel_block_size`, but that identifier appears nowhere else in the tree — it was never implemented.

Instrumented at the indexer, two identical requests, prefix caching off:

| | before | after fix |
|---|---|---|
| distinct cache slots written (of 4096 pools) | **864** | **4096** |
| `max_slot` | 863 (= 26x32+31) | 4159 (= 26x

items.bodyExcerpt:
### The behaviour

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.process_weights_after_loading` fuses `gate_proj` and `up_proj` into `w13` and keeps only the **gate** per-tensor global scale:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L967-L975

```python
# Use a single gscale for w13.
if self.moe.is_act_and_mul and not torch.allclose(
    layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0], layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 1]
):
    logger.warning_once(
        "w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected."
    )
w13_weight_scale_2 = layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0].contiguous()
```

When the two differ, the up-projection half of `w13` is then dequantised with the gate half's global scale. The mismatch is detected, logged once, and the wrong scale is used anyway.

### How far apart they can be

Measured directly from the checkpoints on disk (reading only the `weight_scale_2` scalars — no GPU, no inference):

| checkpoint | modelopt | gate/up pairs | pairs that differ | ratio median / p99 / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4` | 0.45.0 | 12,384 | **8,563 (69.1%)** | 1.077 / 1.69 / **10.0** |

| `mazinb/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-NVFP4` | 0.46.0-compatible-rtn | 24,576 | 0 (0.0%) | — |

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] Sparse-MLA indexer reserves a 32 GiB decode-logits workspace during profiling (max_num_batched_tokens rows), costing 21 % of the KV cache
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

On ROCm, the sparse-MLA indexer reserves the decode logits workspace at the theoretical upper bound during the memory profiling run, not at the bound the scheduler can actually produce. On a 1M-context model that single allocation is **32 GiB per GPU**, and since `WorkspaceManager.lock()` freezes the size after profiling, it is subtracted from the KV cache for the lifetime of the process.

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, profiling early-exit branch of `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`:

```python
# Decode logits buffer, used by rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits.
# batch_size * next_n <= hidden_states.shape[0] == max_num_batched_tokens
if _ON_GFX942 or _ON_GFX950:
    workspace_manager.get_simultaneous(
        ((hidden_states.shape[0], max_model_len), torch.float32),
    )
```

The comment states the bound correctly, but `max_num_batched_tokens` is a *prefill* bound. A decode step produces at most `max_num_seqs * (num_speculative_tokens + 1)` rows — for us 64 · 4 = 256, against the 8192 that get reserved.

## Evidence

Full GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`), TP4 on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, `max_model_len` 1048576, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, `max_num_seqs` 64, MTP k=3, fp8 KV, block size 16.

`torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(context="all", stacks="python")` around `profile_run()`, peak of the profiling run — one allocation dominates everything else:

```
peak 34.18 GiB
  32.00 GiB  n=1   largest 32768.0 MiB
    workspace.py _ensure_workspace_size <- workspace.py get_simultaneous
    <- rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer

   0.19 GiB  n=2   rmsnorm / fused_add_rms_norm

items.bodyExcerpt:
### TL;DR

On GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool sparse indexer, ROCm aiter path), per-layer top-k selection frequently drops the most recent context pools at long prompt lengths — even with a correct block table. The config sets `always_select_tail=True`, but the only tail the selection machinery guarantees is the ≤3-token *incomplete* pool; complete recent pools compete in the top-k like everything else and can rank below the `index_topk=2048` cutoff. Tail-of-context retrieval then fails non-deterministically. Forcing the last 128 pools (512 tokens, 25% of the budget) into every layer's selection fixed all our failing lengths up to the full 256K context.

### Setup

GLM-5.3-Flash-AWQ-W4A16, vLLM `0.31.0.dev0+git73859fec` (Sep-28 pin), TP=2 (ray across 2× AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Strix Halo, gfx1151), aiter sparse MLA, `index_topk` 2048, `index_kpool` 4, `max_model_len` 262144. ## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

## Safety

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.
- Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap.
- The default `index_topk_freq = 1` path is unchanged.
- Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Every DeepSeek-Sparse-Attention layer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, and their MTP drafts) runs a lightweight indexer whose pre-processing costs five kernel launches per layer per step:

1. `LayerNorm` on `k`
2. RoPE on the leading rope dims of `q` and `k`
3. per-token-group FP8 quantization of `q`
4. a pointwise fold of the `q` scale into the indexer `weights`
5. FP8 quantization of `k` plus the paged indexer K-cache write

At decode sizes this is launch-bound: the cost barely moves with token count. AITER already ships a kernel that does all five in one launch (`indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`). This PR wires it in behind a new, default-off env flag `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_INDEXER_QK_FUSION`.

The kernel writes the indexer K cache itself, so the sparse-attention indexer op skips its own insert (`skip_k_cache_insert`). Two data-movement optimizations ride along: the rope `cos_sin_cache` halves are registered once as strided views on the indexer's rotary embedding instead of being re-split every layer every step, and one zero-initialized `q_fp8`/`weights` output pair is shared by the indexer layers of a model (allocated next to `topk_indices_buffer` and sized the same way), with only the first indexer of a forward pass zero-filling it. items.title: [Model] Enable LoRA support for tower and connector in GLM-ASR
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Part of #31479 (LoRA for the tower and connector of more multimodal models).

Enable tower/connector LoRA for GLM-ASR (`GlmAsrForConditionalGeneration`). The audio tower (`GlmAsrEncoder`) and projector (`GlmAsrMultiModalProjector`) are already vLLM-native linear layers and `get_mm_mapping` already maps them, so this PR adds the token-count helpers that the LoRA mapping needs:

- `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` / `get_num_mm_connector_tokens`: every 30s chunk is padded to 3000 mel frames, which the conv stack downsamples to `audio_config.max_position_embeddings` (1500) tower rows; the projector runs on the 4x frame-merged output *before* the padded frames are trimmed, so it sees 375 rows per chunk (also the number of LM tokens a full chunk yields). Only the last chunk of an audio can yield fewer LM tokens, so `num_chunks = ceil(num_audio_tokens / 375)`.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`ModelConfig.is_nvfp4_quantized()` detects NVFP4 by looking for `"nvfp4"` in the quantization config's **top-level** `format` string. Compressed-tensors **mixed-precision** checkpoints declare per-group schemes instead — the top-level format is `"mixed-precision"` and never names nvfp4 even when groups plainly are.

Concrete case: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (`format: "mixed-precision"`, `config_groups.group_1` = W4A4 float, `tensor_group`, `group_size 16`, per-group `format: "nvfp4-pack-quantized"`, targeting `mlp.(gate|up|down)_proj` — 56 of 64 MLP layers). The check returns False → `enable_act_fusion()` returns False → `pass_config.fuse_act_quant` stays False at **every** optimization level → `ActivationQuantFusionPass` never runs → the fused CUDA op `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` is unreachable (it is referenced only from that pass) and Inductor handles silu+mul+fp4-quant — which `enable_act_fusion`'s own docstring says it cannot: *"FP4 quant is always custom so Inductor cannot fuse it."*

Fix: when the top-level format is mixed, inspect `config_groups`. A group counts as NVFP4 if its per-group `format` names nvfp4, **or** it matches the NVFP4 scheme exactly (W4A4 float + `tensor_group` + `group_size 16` + symmetric), mirroring `CompressedTensorsConfig._is_nvfp4_format`. The strictness is load-bearing: **MXFP4 is also W4A4 float** (strategy `group`, group_size 32) — e.g. `INCModel3/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4-Mixed-CT-AutoRound` — and must not be misclassified. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. items.title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Opt-in per-layer overlapped WRITE-push for disaggregated KV transfer
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary / motivation

The stock `NixlConnector` transfers KV as a single, monolithic READ at the end of
prefill, so KV transfer does **not** overlap with prefill compute. On
disaggregated (P/D-split) inference this leaves throughput on the table versus
push-style transports.

This PR adds an **opt-in, per-layer overlapped WRITE-push** path: the prefill
side pushes each layer's KV to the decode worker as soon as that layer is
computed, overlapping KV transfer with the tail of prefill and closing the
throughput gap against push-style connectors — while staying on the open,
standard UCX/NIXL path.

Design notes / rationale live in the commit message and inline docstrings in
`push_worker.py` (module docstring describes the event-driven push pipeline).

## Design

- **Per-layer save hook** (`save_kv_layer`): records a CUDA event per layer and
  enqueues **one RDMA WRITE per KV region off-thread**, so the forward thread is
  never blocked on transfer.
- **Seal** (`wait_for_save`): finalizes the request. A model-agnostic
  **"completeness sweep"** at seal time writes any KV regions **not** covered by
  a per-layer hook (e.g. the GLM-5.1 DSA indexer caches), guaranteeing no stale
  KV is left on the decode side.
- **Scheduler bookkeeping** (`push_scheduler.py`): producer/consumer tracking
  suppresses the monolithic WRITE when layer-wise mode is on, and holds the
  engine loop open until the per-layer WRITEs complete.
- **D-side robustness fixes** (small, independently useful):
  - Seed `remote_*` params on the abort/reject recv path so an aborted/rejected
    request no longer `KeyError`s the EngineCore.
  - Handle `num_external_tokens <= 0` (full prefix-cache hit / no external
    tokens) by flipping `do_remote_prefill` off instead of staging an unseeded
    recv.

- Gated entirely by env var **`VLLM_NIXL_LAYERWISE_PUSH`** (plus
  **`VLLM_NIXL_LAYERWISE_DEFER_TIMEOUT`** for the deferred-write watchdog).

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix GLM-5.3 kpool indexer block sizes
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

  Fixes #54359: GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache.

  On ROCm, GLM-5.3-Flash compresses one indexer state from every
  index_kpool tokens. However, the generic ROCm indexer backend currently
  advertises the following kernel block-size support in token units:

  [1, MultipleOf(16)]

  This allows the complete KV manager block to be selected directly as the
  kernel block size.

  For index_kpool=4 and a 640-token manager block, this selects 640 tokens,
  which represents 160 compressed states. The paged-MQA kernels operate on
  pages of 32 or 64 states, so the block table is not split at the granularity
  used by the kernel.

  As described in
  #54359, this can cause
  multiple logical indexer pages to address the same physical cache slots,
  silently corrupting the indexer cache and degrading long-context retrieval.

  ## Changes

  - Add a cached kpool-aware indexer backend.
  - Scale paged-MQA state page sizes by index_kpool when advertising
    supported kernel block sizes.

  - Use the kpool-aware backend only for Glm5NextIndexerCache on ROCm.
  - Keep the non-ROCm path unchanged.
  - Keep the generic DeepSeek indexer backend unchanged.
  - Add regression coverage for both the 32-state and 64-state page cases.

  For index_kpool=4, the kpool-aware backend advertises:

  32 states × 4 tokens/state = 128 tokens
  64 states × 4 tokens/state = 256 tokens

  This causes the existing hybrid block-table implementation to split the

# [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).
HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls back only the indexer-selected rows just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

## Changes

**Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel.** HiSparse
points attention at a view over the *whole multi-layer KV slab*, so emitted row
indices scale with total block count: max row index is 33 off HiSparse and 7.5M
on. AITER's decode kernel computes `row_index * row_width` in int32, so on
GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above row 3,728,270 and returns approximately
zero — no NaN, no assert. Force Triton kernel for HiSparse for time being. 

**ROCm backend wiring.** CUDA HiSparse backends consume a dense `[tokens, topk]`
tensor; AITER's decode kernel consumes a ragged list plus indptr. Bridging that
is most of the diff: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` registers with an
`index_group_builder` (which is what makes `mla_attention.py` pick up
`hisparse_cache`), decode converts dense physical top-k to ragged and attends
against the hot buffer, and prefill stages host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
when the context is not fully resident. One new Triton kernel,
`compact_topk_to_ragged_triton` — `fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable
because a mid-row `-1` must drop out rather than displace a valid entry.
AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse (its
buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward
time); noted as a perf follow-up.

**HIP kernel port (`csrc/`).** The four fused HiSparse cache ops build and run
on ROCm. Mechanical: vectorized copy widths, `__nv_bfloat16` → `hip_bfloat16`,
warp-primitive shims in `csrc/cuda_compat.h`. CUDA codegen unaffected.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip the seq_lens D2H sync in the AITER sparse MLA metadata key
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

This is the ROCm counterpart of #58684, which has the background.

On every build of `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` with persistent metadata (the default for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x sparse MLA), `seq_lens[:num_reqs].cpu()` runs, decode steps included. That is a blocking D2H copy, and under async scheduling it stalls the CPU until the GPU catches up. The copy only feeds the cache key that decides whether to re-run `get_mla_metadata_v1`, which was added in #42982. The metadata itself is already built on device from `paged_kv_indptr`.

The key only looks at seq_lens and context lens clamped to `index_topk`, so exact values usually aren't needed. This PR builds the key from `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` whenever that gives the same key:
- **No spec decode:** the upper bound is exact, so it's always used.
- **Spec decode:** the bound can overshoot by up to `num_speculative_tokens`. It's used once every request's `context_ub - num_speculative_tokens >= index_topk`. Past that point both lens clamp to `index_topk`, so the key is identical to the exact one. That's the steady state for long-context decode, the same regime #42982 targeted.
- **Otherwise:** it falls back to the current D2H copy.

Unlike #58684, no device fixup is needed, since AITER already plans on device.

Not changed here:
- The `synchronize()` after a metadata recompute (#47404) is untouched. The fast path never recomputes, since the key stays the same.

## Purpose

Fuse Q projection with `fused_q` kernel, removing one separate `torch.bmm` launch per attention layer.

All 78 layers are eligible: **78 fewer GPU kernel launches per TP rank**

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
import torch
import triton

from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.common.kernels import fused_q


@torch.inference_mode()
def benchmark(num_tokens: int) -> None:
    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, 16, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    q_nope, q_pe = q.split([192, 64], dim=-1)
    w_uk_t = torch.randn(512, 16, 192, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).permute(
        1, 2, 0
    )
    index_q = torch.randn(num_tokens, 32, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    index_weights = torch.randn(num_tokens, 32, device="cuda")
    positions = torch.arange(num_tokens, device="cuda")
    rope_cache = torch.randn(max(128, num_tokens), 64, device="cuda")
    q_scale = torch.tensor([0.37], device="cuda")

    def prepare(ql_nope, *, fuse_projection: bool):
        return fused_q(
            positions,
            q_pe,
            rope_cache,
            index_q,
            rope_cache,
            ql_nope,
            q_scale,
            index_weights,
            128**-0.5,
            32**-0.5,
            index_rope_interleave=True,
            quantize_mqa=False,
            q_nope=q_nope if fuse_projection else None,
            w_uk_t=w_uk_t if fuse_projection else None,
        )

    def baseline():
        ql_nope = torch.bmm(q_nope.transpose(0, 1), w_uk_t).transpose(0, 1)
        return ql_nope, *prepare(ql_nope, fuse_projection=False)

        return ql_nope, *prepare(ql_nope, fuse_projection=True)

## Purpose

Fix two independent ways an image request takes down the engine in the GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) vision tower.

**1. Every image trips the GPU sync check.** `rot_pos_emb` builds `pos_ids` on the host and copied it with `.to(device, non_blocking=True)` from pageable memory, and the eager `forward` did the same with `cu_seqlens`. A non-blocking copy from pageable memory can block the host, so with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` the first image raises `Implicit GPU<->CPU sync detected - use a pinned, densely laid out CPU tensor, or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()` and the engine dies.

Fix: stage both copies through pinned memory with `async_tensor_h2d`, as `Glm4vVisionTransformer` does for its position tables. The eager and CUDA-graph forward paths are otherwise unchanged. The `max_seqlen` read-back in the ViT attention wrappers already runs under `gpu_sync_allowed()`, so nothing else in the eager path trips the check.

**2. Slim images overflow the vision rope table.** Since vllm-project/vllm#57387, images go through the transformers `Glm5NextImageProcessor`, whose `smart_resize` bounds them by token budget only, with no aspect-ratio cap. A slim image therefore gets a grid side beyond the hardcoded `max_position=8192`. For example, with the checkpoint's `processor_config.json`, a 200000×20 px image is accepted at 7143 tokens with `image_grid_thw = [1, 2, 14286]`, and `cos[pos_ids]` reads past the table: an `IndexError` on CPU, a device-side assert on GPU.

Fix (suggested in review): size the table from `text_config.max_position_embeddings`. For GLM-5.3-Flash that is 1,048,576 rows, about 64 MiB in bf16 per GPU.

For every grid that fit the old table, the vision tower's output is bit-identical to before.

This supersedes #55543 by @Leoyzen, who is kept as co-author. It enables the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM90 for rope-free sparse-MLA models with head_size 512, such as GLM-5.3-Flash, through `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`.

On H100, plain `fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (with the fix from #55222) holds more tokens. The idea is the same as in #55543: keep the DeepSeek 656B row and leave the RoPE slot at zero. This version keeps all of the logic inside the backend.

items.title: [glm] [pcp] [2/n] add KCP for hybrid GLM KDA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable prefill context parallelism (hybrid PCP) for GLM-5.3's KDA linear-attention layers with KCP, a two-pass parallel scan over each rank's zig-zag prefill segments on FlashKDA kernels:

1. Prepare every local segment once with FlashKDA's preparation kernel.
2. Summarize each segment as an affine map from that workspace: one FlashKDA-derived recurrence over the value columns from a zero state (S) plus the identity's columns with zero input (the transition M). Like FlashKDA's K2 after vllm-project/FlashKDA#13, it keeps the state in FP32 between tiles, and it writes BF16 `[S^T; M^T]` straight into the all-gather buffer.
3. Exchange the summaries in two parts with in-place all-gathers on a side stream, overlapping the next part's summaries and the merge.
4. Merge in chunk order in FP32 (one Triton kernel per part), reading each request's base state from the recurrent cache and writing the final state back; slots no rank has tokens in are skipped.
5. Scan with FlashKDA's K2 from the merged initial states; part-0 segments scan while part 1 is still being gathered, using K2's segment subsets.

The preparation and the scan are FlashKDA's own launches (`launch_fwd` with K1 or K2 alone); only the summary kernel is in vLLM (`csrc/flashkda_kcp.cuh`).

Plumbing:
- `PCPManager.build_hybrid_layout()` returns a model-agnostic per-step layout (decode/prefill rows, each local segment's request, zig-zag slot and token range); Mamba metadata stays on the global batch and each Mamba group binds its state slots once per step.
- The model derives its KCP plan from the layout ahead of the forward via an optional `prepare_hybrid_pcp(layout)` hook, shared by every Mamba group.
- The group coordinator gains a dim-0 in-place all-gather over power-of-two symmetric scratch per key.
- Hybrid PCP rejects speculative decoding, CUDA graphs, non-SM10x devices, a non-FlashKDA KDA prefill backend, and Mamba prefix caching (`mamba_cache_mode != "none"`): KCP does not export Mamba prefill

items.title: [Bugfix][Executor] Size response rings for in-flight batches
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

With Model Runner V2 async scheduling and a KV output aggregator, every worker rank must send a response so the aggregator can observe connector state. The multinode worker response ring is fixed at six slots, while the async pipeline can have multiple in-flight batches. A PP8 async window has nine batches, and a batch can issue both `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` RPCs before EngineCore drains the oldest future. Workers can therefore enter the full-ring polling path during normal execution.

## Change

- Size worker response rings for `2 * max_concurrent_batches` replies.
- Keep the existing ten-slot single-node floor and six-slot multinode floor.
- Thread the multinode capacity through `GroupCoordinator.create_single_reader_mq_broadcasters` as a keyword-only argument.
- Preserve all-rank replies and KV/EC output aggregation semantics.

At PP8 with async scheduling, the multinode ring grows from 6 to 18 slots. This increases the local response-ring shared-memory reservation by 48 MiB per colocated worker (24 MiB to 72 MiB at the current 4 MiB slot size). The single-node floor remains unchanged for PP sizes where the computed window is below ten.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The shared FLA recurrent launchers in `vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/` put the batch x value-head product in `gridDim.z`:

```python
grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)
```

CUDA caps `gridDim.y`/`gridDim.z` at 65535, so any decode (or spec-decode) batch with `N * HV > 65535` fails to launch with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`. For example, 1024 sequences x 64 local value heads, or 2048 x 32. This affects:

- `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd`: Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 GDN decode, OLMo hybrid GDN
- `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`: Qwen GDN decode / spec decode
- `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` in `ops/kda.py`: reuses the same kernel, used by `bailing_moe_v3`

This PR flattens the grid to `grid = (N * HV * NV, NK)`, so `N * HV` lives in `gridDim.x`, whose limit is 2^31 - 1. The kernels recover `i_nh, i_v = pid // NV, pid % NV`, so the V tile varies fastest. This keeps the original launch order: the V tiles of one (sequence, head) stay adjacent and share that head's q/k/g loads in L2. The packed decode kernel in the same file already guards against this limit with `SPLIT_BATCH_HEAD_GRID`. The kernel bodies are otherwise unchanged.

A first version put `N * HV` in X and the V tiles in Y. That spread the V tiles of a head `N * HV` CTAs apart and made KDA decode up to 1.4x slower at large batches; see the benchmark below.

**Not a duplicate:** #56974 fixes the same class of bug, but only in the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA copy (`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/...`). It does not touch these shared files. I found no other open PR that changes the grid of these launchers. #54637 and #51508 touch the same files but not the launch grid.

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

## Overview

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. ## Claims

- The grammar now consumes a reasoning-end token that `ParserEngine.extract_content_ids` keeps as content, if the grammar accepts it. Close tags such as `</think>` are still skipped.

- Under speculative decoding, the mask row at a drafted `<tool_call>` stays unconstrained, so a draft cannot force the end of reasoning. When `<tool_call>` is the last draft, the bonus row is now masked from the grammar state after it.
  - The unit case `inclusive_last` covers this. Its bonus row equals the row after accept, and the grammar then rejects a second `{`. It fails without the fix on both backends.

- The same failure reproduces on Qwen3 (`qwen3` + `hermes`), and the fix removes it there too.
- This does not raise the rate of correct calls on the GLM tool-result prompt. Many recovered responses hit a separate argument bug (see Limitations).

items.title: [Bugfix][Structured Outputs] Keep tool-call openers that end reasoning inside the grammar constraint
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fixes #59608. When reasoning ends on a tool-call opener instead of `</think>` (GLM-4.7/5.x can jump straight from reasoning into `<tool_call>`), the structured-output gate started the grammar constraint one token past the opener. The grammar never saw the opener, so it forced the model to emit a second `<tool_call>`, the parser then dropped the malformed call, and `required`/named tool calls came back empty.

## Claims

- The reasoning-end fast path now distinguishes terminators that are pure reasoning syntax (`</think>`) from terminators that are the first content token (a tool-call opener), using the transition events already declared in each parser config.
- For content terminators the constraint starts at the marker and the marker is fed to the grammar, so the grammar state advances past the opener instead of re-forcing it. Pure terminators keep the existing `offset + 1` behavior.
- Configs affected on main: `glm47_moe` (the `glm45`/`glm47` reasoning parsers), `qwen3`, `gemma4`, `mistral`. Each has a `(REASONING, tool opener)` transition that emits both `REASONING_END` and `TOOL_CALL_START` on a single-token terminal.

## Validation

New unit coverage, all runnable on CPU:

- `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py`: the GLM config derives `reasoning_end_token_ids == {</think>, <tool_call>}` and `reasoning_end_content_token_ids == {<tool_call>}`.
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py`: the multi-token DSML opener stays out of both sets (negative case).

## Overview

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. It covers both the read/write path and low-precision attention arithmetic. items.title: [Bugfix][Quark] Pass grouped-routing arguments to OCP MX monolithic kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.apply_monolithic` does not forward `num_expert_group`, `topk_group`, `e_score_correction_bias` or `routed_scaling_factor` to the monolithic kernel, so the kernel falls back to their defaults.

Quark OCP MX picks its experts through `select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, the same path `Mxfp4MoEMethod` uses. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` has forwarded these four arguments since #50000; the Quark copy, added earlier in #38774, was never updated.

**Who is affected.** The bug needs three things at once:

1. A Quark **weight-only MXFP4 (`w_mxfp4`, W4A16)** checkpoint.
2. DeepSeek-V3/V4-style routing (grouped top-k and/or a correction bias with a scaling factor).
3. A **monolithic** MXFP4 kernel. On SM100, the BF16-activation priority list selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` (`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, which supports `DeepSeekV3` routing) by default. On ROCm, `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` (`DeepSeekV3`/`DeepseekV4`) is used when requested explicitly.

In that setup the kernel routes with `n_group=0`, `topk_group=0` and no bias, and the scaling factor is `None` (TRT-LLM) or 1.0 (aiter).

The published Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints are W4A4: `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4`, `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4`, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4` and others. W4A4 resolves to the modular `AiterExperts` on ROCm and to emulation on CUDA, so routing happens in vLLM's router with every argument. As far as I can tell, no public checkpoint hits this today. This PR fixes a latent inconsistency before a W4A16 export does.

This PR forwards the four arguments exactly as `Mxfp4MoEMethod` does. Models without grouped routing pass `None` or the default values and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy).
- Code-path analysis above (`oracle/mxfp4.py` activation filtering and priority lists). There is no public W4A16 Quark checkpoint to run end to end.

## Test Result

`pre-commit` passes. Related: #59757 moves the monolithic kernel

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step.

The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path.

## Claims

- Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.
- No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint.

## Validation

Setup: RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on 2 H200 GPUs, served with default settings plus MTP:

```

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

This PR routes the GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) fused QKV-A projection
through the existing `min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj` custom op backed by
`dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, eliminating the cuBLASLt split-K + splitKreduce kernel pair
at decode batch size 1. The `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` C++ kernel already supports the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A shape with a warp-specialized fused-A kernel that folds the
split-K reduction inside the CTA -- the same kernel SGLang uses for this projection.
The custom op has a registered `fake_impl`, making it torch.compile-safe and CUDA-graph
capture-safe.

The core change widens `_can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm` to accept the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A weight shape alongside the existing DeepSeek-V3 shape. This
collapses two kernel launches per layer (splitK GEMM + splitKreduce) into a single
`fused_a_gemm_kernel` launch. PDL (Programmatic Dependent Launch) is also enabled on
SM90+ for additional latency reduction at low token counts.

Because the fused-QKV-A custom-op path is frozen into the CUDA graph at capture time,
the GLM-5.2 branch is gated on the `VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM`
kill switch so the feature-toggle A/B comparison captures the full benefit of this path

items.title: [Bugfix][Model] GLM-5.x: load ModelOpt NVFP4 MLA projections into BF16 fused_qkv_a_proj
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_qkv_a_proj` in GLM-5.x (`glm5next`) is always BF16, and the loader only knows how to dequantize FP8 checkpoints into it (`_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`). A ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint that also quantizes the MLA projections stores `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` as a packed e2m1 `weight` (uint8), an e4m3 per-16 `weight_scale` and an fp32 `weight_scale_2`. Those tensors have no matching parameter, so loading fails:

```
vllm/model_executor/parameter.py, in load_merged_column_weight
    assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape
AssertionError
```

Example checkpoint: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16; MoE experts, dense MLPs and the MLA `q_a`/`q_b`/`kv_a`/`o` projections are NVFP4; KDA, `kv_b_proj`, routers and norms stay BF16).

## Changes

- `_try_load_nvfp4_attn_proj`: buffers `weight`, `weight_scale` and `weight_scale_2` per projection, then dequantizes with the existing `dequantize_to_dtype(..., swizzle=False)` and loads the BF16 result into the fused shard. It only acts when the target has no `weight_scale` param, so projections the model keeps in NVFP4 (here `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`) load as before.
- Called before the FP8 path in both the main model and the MTP layer, because the FP8 path now also accepts `.weight_scale` (Quark). It only claims uint8 weights and e4m3 scales, so FP8 and BF16 tensors are untouched.
- The NoPE `kv_a` row padding and fused-shard load move into a small shared helper, `_load_bf16_attn_proj`, used by both paths.

## Not a duplicate

No open or merged PR or issue covers NVFP4 MLA projections in the GLM-5.x loader (searched `fused_qkv_a_proj nvfp4`, `glm5next nvfp4 q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa nvfp4`, the assertion text). The scale mismatch in NVFP4 MoE experts (#54974, #55073) is a separate issue.

items.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] NVFP4 linear: keep each fused shard's global weight scale
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`KNvfp4Static.process` runs a fused NVFP4 linear (`q/k/v`, `gate/up`) under the max of its shards' global weight scales (`weight_scale_2`), and only warns when they differ. Every smaller shard is then dequantized `gs_max / gs_shard` times too large. ModelOpt quantizes each projection with its own per-tensor amax, so fused shards often do differ.

Example: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16) quantizes the shared experts and dense MLPs. Their gate/up global scales differ in nearly every MoE layer, with up/gate ratios from 0.46 to 2.51 across a layer sample, so one projection is inflated by up to 2.5x in every layer for every token. Greedy output stays coherent, which is why this hides. Sampled output at the checkpoint's own defaults (temperature 1, top_p 0.95) degenerates into multilingual word salad within a few hundred tokens.

## Changes

- `_reconcile_nvfp4_shard_global_scales`: before the shared max is taken, each smaller shard's e4m3 block scales are multiplied by `gs_shard / gs_max`.
  - The factor is at most 1, so block scales cannot overflow.
  - Each shard keeps its effective dequant scale within e4m3 rounding.
  - The FP4 payload is unchanged.
- Shared-scale checkpoints are bit-exact no-ops. The previous warning remains for layers whose shard widths (`logical_widths`) cannot be verified against `weight_scale`.
- This is the same policy as FP8's `requantize_with_max_scale` for fused linears, and as #55073 for NVFP4 MoE w13. #55073 does not touch the linear path.

This PR covers the **ModelOpt** path (`KNvfp4Static`, shared by W4A4 and W4A16), which #47515 does not touch.
